Authority: the request names the project as the target, which grants edits to this repo's files; it grants no commit, push, PR, release or deploy and no new dependency (assumption, Q8, Q11). Consumers and entry points: HTTP clients of the existing list route via its query string, plus any in-repo caller or test of that route, which discovery finds (Q1). Actors: HTTP clients with no identity; assumption: no auth, so every caller sees the same list (Q7). Shared state: one process-wide in-memory store shared by all callers and sessions; its lifetime is the process and a restart ends it (fact from 'in-memory', details unverified). Pagination holds no server-side state, so concurrent writes can shift pages. Hidden fields: none assumed beyond today's behaviour, which stays unchanged. Already provided by the runtime: Node's HTTP stack and the store, to be verified.\nWhere and when visible: the outcome is the behaviour of the list endpoint in src/server.js.
